subject: Re: MAP & POC environment — org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Eve Soto <eve.soto@clearhealth.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP & POC kickoff — network and keys questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to a short POC. Before we lock in dates, can you confirm the exact items you need from our side to stand up the MAP POC environment (org, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)? We want to avoid any last-minute surprises.

Quick context: we plan to run a 2-week eval against a subset of production-like traffic (anonymized) and need predictable activation time. Raj (cc'd on future messages) will lead infra.

Main asks from our side: what formats do you need for peering (ASN/CIDR), do you require a dedicated org or just a project-level token, and any expected maintenance windows for peering?

Would like to aim for a mid-Nov activation if possible.

Thanks,
Eve Soto
Head of Product
ClearHealth

---
Attachments: none
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
To: Eve Soto <eve.soto@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & POC kickoff — network and keys questions

Hi Eve — thanks for the clear list. Outline below is the minimal set we need to activate the MAP POC environment and validate readiness. I attached our short MAP checklist (redwood-map-checklist-v1.pdf) as a one-pager.

Summary of what we need from ClearHealth
- Org setup: a dedicated Redwood evaluation org is preferred so we can apply rate limits and isolation. If you prefer a project-level token, confirm the project id and service account.
- API keys: one scoped evaluation API key + one mgmt key for streaming logs. We provide token rotation guidance in the attachment.
- IP allowlist: sample JSON schema attached (ip-allowlist-sample.json). Please provide the public egress IPs you will use for the test runners and the CIDR for any NATs.
- VPC peering: we support standard peering (BGP optional). We'll need your VPC CIDR, preferred peering windows, and ASN if you want BGP. See peering-template.yaml for the required fields.

Proposed timeline
- Nov 6: Exchange keys and allowlist JSON
- Nov 8–10: VPC peering test window (low-risk maintenance)
- Nov 13: Dry run (connectivity + auth test)
- Nov 14: Go-live for 2-week eval (start of measurement period)

Next steps: Raj, can you confirm the VPC CIDR and whether you want BGP? If you share the IP list, Marissa will configure the allowlist and Marcus will provision the peering on our side.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood-map-checklist-v1.pdf, ip-allowlist-sample.json
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@clearhealth.ai>, Eve Soto <eve.soto@clearhealth.ai>, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Technical details — sample allowlist + peering template

Hi Raj / Eve — looping in Marcus who will own the peering setup on Redwood's infra. Per Naomi's note, attached are two small artifacts: peering-template.yaml (fields we need) and a sample ip-allowlist-sample.json with the format we ingest into our console.

Quick callouts:
- For the allowlist we accept single IPs or /27+/26 CIDRs. Please include any egress NATs and CI runner ranges.
- If you opt for BGP, provide your ASN and a preferred BGP MD5 key (we support optional auth). If not, static routes are fine for the duration of the eval.
- Peering window: we recommend a 2–3 hour low-traffic window for the initial BGP session bring-up; connectivity tests are non-invasive.

Example lines from the sample allowlist:
- {"label": "ci-runners", "cidrs": ["203.0.113.0/27"]}

If you can send the actual CIDRs and ASN today, Marcus will provision the remote config and I will update the MAP checkpoint sheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: peering-template.yaml, ip-allowlist-sample.json
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@clearhealth.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, eve.soto@clearhealth.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical details — sample allowlist + peering template

Thanks — apologies for the slight delay. Here are the requested items:
- VPC CIDR: 10.44.0.0/16
- Public egress NAT CIDRs: 34.201.12.0/24, 34.201.13.0/24
- ASN: 64512 (we can run BGP)
- Preferred peering window: Nov 8 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic for us)

We prefer BGP so routes update automatically. We will share a one-time MD5 key privately (I'll send via our secure channel).

Two clarifications:
1) Do you require a dedicated org? We can create one, but if token-scoped access is easier we can provide a project/service account.
2) Any expectations on peering egress rules (NAT behavior) during the eval window?

Thanks,
Raj Patel
Infra Lead, ClearHealth

- VPC peering: Marcus completed the initial config; we'll perform the BGP bring-up tonight during your requested window.

Action items for ClearHealth
- Raj: please send the MD5 key via the secure channel before 23:00 UTC tonight.
- Eve: review and e-sign the activation terms (DocuSign link below) so we can finalize access.

DocuSign: https://docs.docusign.com/sign/ABC-Activation-Terms

We'll mark the MAP milestone as "Activation" once the BGP session is ESTABLISHED and the first auth request succeeds. I will follow up after the bring-up with logs.

Thanks everyone — excited to get this running.

Naomi Feldman
